title: Open extension and scalar restriction preserve the normalized scalar counit
statement:
Let $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion of schemes and $A\to B$ a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Use ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ of constant-ring module sheaves, for $W=X,Z$ and $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Put $T_W=-\otimes^L_{A_W}B_W$ and let $r_W$ be exact scalar restriction, with the representative-normalized adjunction $T_W\dashv r_W$ and counit $\epsilon_W$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Write $J_R=j_{!,R}$ for the sheafified extension-by-zero construction [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and its exact derived adjunction $J_R\dashv j_R^{-1}$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Let $a_L:J_Ar_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}r_ZJ_BL$ be the canonical sectionwise restriction-of-scalars comparison of that node. Let $E_M:T_ZJ_AM\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT_XM$ be the canonical open tensor comparison, normalized by its balanced tensor map on the open, as in [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison].
The unit $M\to j_R^{-1}J_RM$ is the identity under the sectionwise identification on objects over $X$, for every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$; in particular restriction to $X$ determines a derived arrow with source $J_RM$ through this adjunction. Under these unit identifications and the canonical restriction/tensor and restriction/scalar identifications, $j_B^{-1}E_M$ and $j_A^{-1}a_L$ are identity comparisons. For every ambient $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ one has the scalar counit equation
$$\epsilon_Z(J_BL)\circ T_Z(a_L)=J_B(\epsilon_X(L))\circ E_{r_XL}.$$
The isomorphisms $a,E$ and this equation are natural in their derived arguments. For the identity ring homomorphism they are the identity comparisons under the canonical scalar unitors. These assertions require no flatness of $B/A$, boundedness, constructibility or Tor condition on $L$ or $r_XL$.

proof.text: Write $u_R=j_R^{-1}$ and $\eta^R:1\to u_RJ_R$ for the open unit. Apply [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] to the constant ring sheaf $R_Z$ on the small pro-etale site and the open $j$, for $R=A,B$. It gives the actual section-normalized isomorphism $\eta^R$, on the ordinary unbounded derived category. Thus $u_RJ_R$ is identified with the identity using $(\eta^R)^{-1}$. In particular the adjunction bijection sends $h:J_RM\to N$ to $u_R(h)\eta^R_M$. Hence two such arrows with equal restrictions are equal, by injectivity of that bijection. This is a statement about arrows with source $J_RM$, not faithfulness of restriction on the ambient derived category.

proof.text: The scalar restriction isomorphism of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], in the orientation $a:J_Ar_X\to r_ZJ_B$, is induced by the identity of the extension presheaves after forgetting the $B$-action. Over an object factoring through $X$, both presheaves have the same module and the map is the identity; their restrictions to the open are already sheaves. The sheafification universal property therefore identifies $u_A(a_L)$ with the identity, under $u_A r_Z=r_Xu_B$ and the units of step 1. Applying this degreewise and localizing preserves this equality, since these are the exact, degreewise-derived functors in that node. This also establishes the naturality of $a$.

proof.text:
Put $\lambda:u_BT_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Xu_A$ for canonical restriction/tensor balancing. The comparison in [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison] is defined by the common right adjoint. Apply [lem-fix-open-scalar-tensor-normalization] to this same finite-ring, ordinary unbounded pro-etale datum: its $\beta_j$ has exactly that definition, and its inverse is the open adjunct of $\lambda^{-1}T_X(\eta^A)$. It identifies this comparison with the balanced open tensor comparison. Consequently, by taking that open transpose and using the units of step 1,
$$u_B(E_M)=\lambda_{J_AM}$$
under $u_AJ_A\cong1$ and $u_BJ_B\cong1$. In particular $u_B(E_M)$ is the identity comparison under the specified tensor identifications. All maps here are the specified comparisons, rather than a freely chosen natural isomorphism.

proof.text:
Let $H\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ and let $\rho_H:u_Ar_ZH\xrightarrow{\sim}r_Xu_BH$ be the identity-on-actions comparison. By [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], $\theta=\lambda^{-1}:T_Xu_A\to u_BT_Z$ is precisely the scalar-adjunction mate of $\rho$ for the representative-normalized scalar adjunctions. In the mate definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], take $L_1=T_Z$, $R_1=r_Z$, $L_2=T_X$, $R_2=r_X$, $G=u_A$, $H=u_B$, and $\alpha=\theta$. The equivalent transpose formula in that definition gives the actual equality
$$u_B(\epsilon_Z(H))\circ\lambda^{-1}_{r_ZH}=\epsilon_X(u_BH)\circ T_X(\rho_H).$$
This is valid for every unbounded $H$: the cited normalization theorem expressly makes no flatness assumption. In particular it does not replace the derived counit by underived multiplication on an arbitrary representative.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; agent use of the scalar mate transpose formula with the canonical balanced restriction comparison.

proof.text:
Let $f=\epsilon_Z(J_BL)\circ T_Z(a_L)$ and $g=J_B(\epsilon_X(L))\circ E_{r_XL}$. Restrict $f$ using $\lambda$ and its naturality, and then use step 4 with $H=J_BL$. Under the open unit identifications this reads
$$u_B(f)=\epsilon_X(L)\circ T_X(\rho_{J_BL}\circ u_A(a_L))=\epsilon_X(L),$$
because step 2 identifies the map in parentheses with the identity. Step 3 gives $u_B(g)=\epsilon_X(L)$ as well. To conclude, precompose both $f$ and $g$ by $E_{r_XL}^{-1}:J_BT_Xr_XL\to T_ZJ_Ar_XL$. Their restrictions remain equal, so step 1's open-adjunction injectivity gives $fE^{-1}=gE^{-1}$. Cancel this isomorphism to obtain the asserted counit equation.

source.place: Agent assembly of steps 1-4; the restriction test is applied only after identifying the source with an open extension.

proof.text: The map $a$ is natural by step 2. The common-right-adjoint comparison $E$ is natural by [lem-fix-open-scalar-tensor-normalization]; scalar counits are natural by their adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Thus the displayed equality is an equality of natural transformations. For $A\xrightarrow{1}A$, $a$ is the identity sectionwise, and $E$ is the identity under scalar unitors by the identity normalization in [lem-fix-open-scalar-tensor-normalization]. The representative formulas $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ and $p\otimes a\mapsto ap$ in the scalar adjunction identify its counit with the scalar unitor in this case, so the equation becomes the identity equation. The arguments used only finite commutative rings and arbitrary unbounded derived objects. In particular $r_XL$ need not be K-flat or have finite Tor amplitude. Empty opens, the whole open $X=Z$, and zero complexes obey the same formulas (zero sources in the empty case).
